content:
maria.gomez: Heads up — we've been getting a lot of noisy alerts from prometheus about node_exporter target failures on the gpu fleet since last night. Appears to be FD exhaustion on several nodes.
kevin.liu: any logs? which nodes?
maria.gomez: n-gpu-03, n-gpu-07, n-gpu-12 so far. From syslog:
```
Mar 17 22:03:12 n-gpu-03 node_exporter[2145]: accept4(3) failed: Too many open files
Mar 17 22:03:12 n-gpu-03 systemd[1]: node_exporter.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Mar 17 22:03:12 n-gpu-03 systemd[1]: Unit node_exporter.service entered failed state.
```
sanjay.patel: interesting — dcgm exporter seems unaffected, and GPU metrics are still visible via the runtime sidecar. This looks specific to node_exporter or the small metrics-forwarder sidecars we rolled last week.
olivia.hart: I just saw prometheus scrape backlog spike in the fleet dashboard: scrape_duration_seconds p95 went to ~3s and queued_targets jumped. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/fleet-scrapes
kevin.liu: that backlog would cause more concurrent connections during retries. Could be a feedback loop: exporter gets slow, more scrape time, more open sockets, hit FD limit, exporter restarts, alert fires.
maria.gomez: quick mitigation: I pushed a change to systemd LimitNOFILE=65536 on the affected nodes and restarted node_exporter on the three. FD usage dropped. Not a root fix though.
infra-bot: deploy-bot reports: rolling restart triggered for node_exporter on n-gpu-03,n-gpu-07,n-gpu-12 by maria.gomez at 2026-03-17T22:15:00Z
sanjay.patel: dug into the metrics-forwarder sidecar logs — it opens a new TCP connection per batch and doesn't always close on context cancellation. Sample stacktrace:
```
metrics-forwarder: 2026-03-17T21:59:58Z WARN open connection leak: fd=1023 remote=10.0.12.5:4210
metrics-forwarder: 2026-03-17T22:00:10Z ERROR failed to flush: context canceled
metrics-forwarder: 2026-03-17T22:00:10Z DEBUG connection 1023 still open after cancel
```
kevin.liu: that pattern will definitely leak FDs under scrape pressure. Also noticed our Prometheus scrape timeout is 10s and we have aggressive scrape_interval=15s for node_exporter — retries could overlap. We should bump scrape_timeout to 7s or increase scrape_interval for noisy targets.
maria.gomez: I've opened a PR to change the forwarder to reuse a connection pool with idle timeouts. PR: https://git.redwood.example/r/infra/metrics-forwarder/pull/448
olivia.hart: I'm going to roll back the sidecar image on a canary set (n-gpu-*/zone-b) to the previous tag while the PR gets reviewed. K8s job queued.
deploy-bot: rollback job started: k8s rolling update metrics-forwarder -> v1.3.2 on namespace=gpu-fleet (canary)
kevin.liu: also propose a short-term alert tuning: suppress pager if node_exporter restarts > 5 times within 1 hour and instead create a SEV2 ticket. We get pager fatigue for noisy infra issues.
maria.gomez: agree. I'll add a mute rule and a runbook note in the alert definition. Runbook snippet:
```
- If node_exporter restarted >5/hr: set alert severity=SEV2, add annotation: "auto-silenced: investigate FD leak, check metrics-forwarder and systemd LimitNOFILE"
- Check `lsof -p <pid>` and `ss -s` for socket counts
- If high backlog: increase scrape_timeout temporarily and scale prometheus scrape relays
```
olivia.hart: after rollback on canary, canary FD counts normalized within a minute. We'll proceed to roll the rest of the zones if tests pass.
sanjay.patel: next steps: 1) merge connection-pool PR, 2) gradual rollout of fixed sidecar, 3) update prometheus scrape timeout & relabel rules to drop super high-cardinality ephemeral metrics, 4) add alert silencing rule and runbook.
maria.gomez: I'll take 1 and 4. Kevin can you handle 3?
kevin.liu: yep, will open a PR to prometheus config to adjust scrape_timeout to 7s for node_exporter and add relabeling to drop metrics matching kube_pod_ips or other ephemeral labels causing extra cardinality.
maria.gomez: thanks all. Filing a short postmortem once the rollout completes. For now, pager noise reduced and affected nodes are stable. :thumbsup:
kevin.liu: add note to capacity planning — we should audit typical FD headroom on gpu nodes and ensure OOM/kube evictions don't mask this.
olivia.hart: noted, will add to next infra sprint.
maria.gomez: closing the incident channel, will update when rollback + fix fully deployed.
_extra: This thread documents an operational incident and the coordination to fix a file descriptor leak affecting node_exporter and a metrics-forwarder sidecar. Messages are short and conversational to reflect Slack style.
